title: Void Pointers
concept: A void pointer contains an address independent of the type, but correct type conversion is essential when using it.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation:
The main frame is created.

This lesson examines the versatility and limitations of `void*`.

steps.title: variable declaration
steps.explanation:
Prepare values ​​of different types, such as `int a` and `float b`.

The same void pointer points to both types alternately.

steps.title: void pointer declaration
steps.explanation:
`void *ptr` is a general-purpose pointer that holds an untyped address.

Direct dereferencing is not possible and requires casting.

steps.title: Storing the address of an int variable
steps.explanation:
Store the int address as `ptr = &a;`.

A void pointer can be assigned various type addresses.

steps.title: Dereference after casting (int)
steps.explanation: After specifying the type with `(int*)ptr`, read the int value by dereferencing it.

steps.title: Storing the address of a float variable
steps.explanation: In the same `ptr`, this time we save the address of `b` and change the target type.

steps.title: Dereferencing (float) after type conversion (Casting)
steps.explanation:
After casting to `(float*)ptr`, read the float value by dereferencing it.

Casting other than the actual type will produce incorrect results.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
Exit with `return 0;`.

Bottom line: void pointers are flexible for storage, but require precise type information to read/write.

quiz.question: What operations are impossible on void pointer ptr?
quiz.explanation: Because the void pointer does not know the target size (byte size), it cannot be directly dereferenced (*ptr) without casting.

misconceptions.wrong: Any value can be placed in void * (e.g. int, float value itself).
misconceptions.correct:
Only 'address' can be entered.
If you enter the value itself, the value is interpreted as an address.
misconceptions.why: A pointer variable is not a container for a value, but rather an arrow pointing to a location.

keyTakeaway: Void pointers are essential when hiding data types and writing generalized code (e.g. memcpy, qsort).
